author: Khaosyr
text:
just after writing this, I found solana:3bHzNdUb9Ko2EZyYvg2okPHQt1tJP8CFLZfkKrvBNtAc which is already a decent example of the sort of interesting dynamics I meant could emerge.

It reflects $STONK, but is now adding programmatic solana:8RVBk8vxLiUHueLUW1f4izFVqN3nWippLhkohKg6EGkS drops too. So instead of just:

solana:3bHzNdUb9Ko2EZyYvg2okPHQt1tJP8CFLZfkKrvBNtAc -> $STONK

you also get:

solana:3bHzNdUb9Ko2EZyYvg2okPHQt1tJP8CFLZfkKrvBNtAc -> solana:8RVBk8vxLiUHueLUW1f4izFVqN3nWippLhkohKg6EGkS -> $STONK

and the whole framing is basically more stonks in the top 10

That's the part of the graph idea I find interesting. Once enough nodes exist, new coins have existing stuff to build with. They can plug into one token, multiple tokens, create new loops, reinforce existing branches or eventually connect things that were previously separate.

And this is also where I think stonk can start building a moat that isn't just the normal launchpad liquidity/user moat.

The reflection mechanic itself is obviously copyable. The interesting bit is if stonk becomes the place where all these relationships actually form. More established nodes gives the next experiment more things to build on, which gives the experiment after that even more things to build on.

The moat isn't that nobody can copy the mechanics. It's that once the graph has enough coins, liquidity, holders and existing relationships, this becomes the obvious place to create the next edge.

solana:3bHzNdUb9Ko2EZyYvg2okPHQt1tJP8CFLZfkKrvBNtAc is a few days old so obviously not saying this proves anything, but this is basically what I meant by cool dynamics emerging from the graph rather than everything just being another isolated launch

author: Dr___Salt
text:
STONK: UNDER SIEGE

I’ve been thinking about where @LaunchOnSF goes from here.

Not because I think the thesis is dead.
Quite the opposite, I think Stonk has already proven the first part of its thesis.
The question now is whether there is a second chapter.

The original thesis was simple:
People are tired of https://t.co/xihwP0vrNO’s extraction.
Stonk offers a different model.
Instead of endlessly launching memes, you can launch a token against anything;

-Crypto.
-Stocks.
-Pre-IPO.
-Sports.
-Collectibles.
-Brands.
-Other tokens.

And the market validated it. Stonk went above 300m. ZCAT, paired with Zcash, went above 100m. Multiple other ecosystem tokens reached 20m, 30m, 40m and 50m+.
There were launches around Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceX, Pokémon, PSG, Coca-Cola, McDonald’s, Hims, leveraged BTC, SOL, HYPE, ZEC, LINK and plenty more.

This wasn’t just people buying the Stonk token because they liked the story.

People actually used the product. The first thesis was proven.
But now comes the harder question.
Have we run out of narratives?

The first wave had an enormous advantage. The underlying assets already had attention.
You didn’t need to explain why Zcash was interesting. You didn’t need to explain SpaceX, Pokémon or OpenAI.

Stonk simply gave people a mechanism to turn existing attention into speculation.

But eventually you get through the obvious ones.

BTC. SOL. HYPE. ZEC. LINK. Anthropic. OpenAI. SpaceX. Pokémon. PSG. The major brands.
Even the penny stocks have already had their moment.

Eventually the next launch becomes:
“Here’s a token paired with a company nobody has heard of.” That’s a very different proposition.
The underlying narrative is no longer generating the demand. The token has to create it. And that’s much harder.

Maybe we misundersto @Pumpfun 

This is where I think the Pump situation gets interesting.
When Pump made moves that looked similar to Stonk, everyone assumed they were coming for the castle.

solana:6GmAFSYs4gk3FDao5FzzySQpPZaWsa4rUJHacpMpUNgx sold off.
Then recovered and eventually went to 300m+.

But maybe Pump never needed to storm the castle. Maybe they could just lay siege to it.
In a siege, you don’t have to attack the walls. You surround the castle. Cut off the supply lines. Wait.

Eventually the defenders run out of food. The walls can still be standing. It doesn’t matter.

The castle starves itself. Maybe that’s what happened here. 
Stonk’s greatest strength was its reflexive flywheel:

More launches → more volume → more fees → more buybacks → more attention → more launches.

For a few days that meant roughly $1m of daily buybacks.
Incredible on the way up. But reflexivity works both ways.

Less volume → fewer fees → fewer buybacks → less attention → fewer launches → less volume.

Pump doesn’t necessarily have to beat Stonk. They just need to remain the dominant place where people launch while Stonk has to continuously find new reasons for people to come back.

That’s why this pullback matters
The first big pullback was mostly about uncertainty.
“Pump is coming.”

This one is different. The volume has actually fallen. The launches aren’t as interesting.
A lot of new tokens are duds. Fees have fallen. Buybacks have fallen. The ecosystem is quieter.

That’s a much better test of the thesis. Because you can’t FUD your way out of declining demand. You need new demand. I don’t think the bear case is necessarily Stonk going to zero. 
The more interesting bear case is that it becomes background infrastructure on Solana.
It keeps operating. People keep launching. Every so often something runs to 20m, 50m or 100m.
But Stonk itself stops being the narrative. 
Maybe it settles around 50m-150m. Maybe it occasionally catches another wave back toward 300m.

That’s not failure.
But it’s very different from the 1b-5b thesis many people are making.

reason.quote: The first big pullback was mostly about uncertainty. This one is different. The volume has actually fallen.
reason.inference: bullish original thesis but bearish on near-term momentum and demand
